about_this_file: The one record of who we are, what is offered and what has been shown. Every surface (tool text, text index, price file, discovery files, pages) is generated from canon/names.json, this file, canon/promise.json and canon/tools.json. Each fact appears once, with its source and the date it was last read. Changes go through its owner.

identity.one_sentence: We're building one app where a person answers every AI in their life, and the people around them, on an open standard any service can brand and anyone can build an app for. Today {network} lets your AIs ask you on your phone: an approval, a choice or a quick answer, each under the name you gave it, free. An agent can also ask its user's own people, and gets back each answer with a record of what that person's page observed.
identity.longer: An agent needs something only a person can give: what a song feels like, whether a game is fun, which of two pages is clearer in ten seconds. It makes one tool call saying who it needs, what they should do, what it pays and by when. Matching people are rung, each does the thing on a phone in a page that records what happened, and the agent gets back each person's answer with that record. On a paid call each person is paid; on every call each person keeps a signed receipt.
is_not: Not a way to reach your own user through a call to people. If your user wants you to ask them, they connect you (https://%%SITE%%/connect) and you ask them through that connection, free; otherwise ask them directly.
Not for facts a search can find, or for work a model can do alone.
Not for anything a person must do away from a screen.
Not a way to get opinions from a model. The simulated people, the default during the preview, are a free test mode: their answers are made up, and every one is marked simulated.
Not a hiring marketplace: a call is minutes of several people's attention, not a job.

three_things.standard: {standard}: an open definition of the call that anyone may implement, under the Apache License 2.0; version 0.1 is a draft.
three_things.software: Software that runs it (the router an agent talks to, the page a person opens when rung, adapters to pools of people, and a conformance suite), to be published as open source. Not yet public.
three_things.network: The hosted router, at the API address in the discovery file, with the pools behind it. This is the part that will charge a fee.

terms.max_total: Every call states max_total_usd, the most it may cost. It must cover the quote's total: the people's pay, every fee and the reserve held for anyone who takes longer (the unused reserve comes back). The call opens only if that total is at or under max_total_usd and under the key's caps. Otherwise nothing opens and the quote comes back.
terms.over_cap: A call over a key's cap opens nothing and returns the price and a link where the human can approve it.
terms.what_you_pay: Always within max_total_usd: people who finished, at the quoted pay; people who stopped, for their time; each fee on those amounts; nothing for people never rung.
terms.short: If fewer people answer than asked, you pay for those who answered and anyone who stopped partway; anyone still in a seat at the deadline may finish and is paid in full; the rest of the hold returns.
terms.cancel: On cancel, nobody new is rung; people already in a seat may finish and are paid in full.
terms.overrun: A person who takes longer than estimated is topped up to the floor from the reserve; past the reserve the operator bears it; never above max_total_usd.
terms.hold: The unused hold returns to the balance when the call closes, and the result says how much.
terms.no_rejection: No asker can reject a person's work. A response is counted by itself 24 hours after it arrives; pay is withheld only on proof of fraud, shown to the person, with an appeal.
terms.retries: Every request that changes something carries an idempotency key; a repeat returns the first result.
terms.errors: Errors are JSON with code, message and fixable; when fixable, the field and a corrected example.
terms.price_changes: Changes to the price are published 30 days ahead in the price file.

how_it_starts.value: An agent can price a call and make simulated calls with no key and no money. A free test key adds a balance and caps. Real people are rung only on a panel whose members joined it themselves, from its join link on their own phones; any key can make one, a free test key too. The one exception is the front page's demo (Call me), which rings the visitor themselves with one of a few fixed asks.

how_it_ends.value: A call closes at its deadline, when everyone asked has answered, or when the asker cancels. What came in is returned with the unspent part of the hold.

preview_means: What "preview" means: what works now is real. Your own AIs ask you, and your own people answer your calls, for free. Strangers are not offered yet, so any money you see is test money only: nothing is charged and nobody is paid until a stranger pool opens. Until then, a stand-in for strangers is open to any test key (its pool is named in the discovery file, under strangers_stand_in): scripted stand-ins answer in seconds, every answer is marked simulated, and nobody at the pool is asked or paid. person.tools is run by Hammer Corp., Austin, Texas.
own_ai_difference: How this differs from a notification app (ntfy, Telegram or Home Assistant are free, older and fine for an alert): your answer goes back to your AI as data it can act on (the choice you picked, the exact text you approved, and when); all your AIs reach you in one place, each under its own name, and any one can be revoked, quieted or blocked with one tap; you set when you can be asked; and nothing an AI sends you is read by anyone at person.tools.
